translations.text: Gregory of Rome, the man of grace, thought about the hidden sins of people, which they would not confess.
He wept to God and poured out a prayer to Him, asking that the way in which they might be [?] (perhaps 'healed' or 'atoned for') be revealed to him. An angel came to him and said to him:
'Your sorrow is great, and I have come from God to comfort you. As for the person you are concerned about,
let him make his confession before God and His creatures, and let him shed tears, and let this be what he sings':

'Domine, quis habitabit' ('Lord, who shall dwell'), 'Domini est terra' ('The earth is the Lord's'), 'Te decet' ('Praise is due to you'), 'Deus, in nomine' ('O God, in your name'), 'Deus misereatur' ('May God be merciful'),

and 'Deus in adiutorium' ('O God, come to my help') as far as 'Festina' ('make haste') between every two psalms, and 'Appropinquatur' [?], and the 'Pater' (the Lord's Prayer), and 'Ascendat usque ad thronum' ('May it ascend to the throne').
'Is there another?' said Gregory. 'There is,' said the angel.
Three psalms, namely: 'Dominus illuminatio' ('The Lord is my light'), 'Judica, Domine, nocentes' ('Judge, O Lord, those who harm me'), and 'Exurgat' ('Let God arise').

These three psalms protect against envy, demons and harms, provided they are sung every day, with 'Deus in adiutorium' ('O God, come to my help') as far as 'Festina' ('make haste') between every two psalms, and the 'Pater' (the Lord's Prayer).

If it is an urgent [?] prayer (dían-adrige), two psalms and a canticle: 'Confitemini Domino' ('Give thanks to the Lord'), 'In aeternum' ('For ever'), 'Super flumina' ('By the rivers'), and the 'Benedicite', and 'Ante faciem tuam' ('Before your face') as far as 'Confirma me' ('Strengthen me').
There is no sin that anyone commits in the body that these commutations do not heal, except blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
